# LLM Cost Tracking and Control

Dimension 4 of the LLM Token Budgeting research. Covers per-request cost
attribution, budget alerts, rate limiting by cost, and observability platforms.
Source details in [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Cost Attribution Architecture

Four components required for cost control [23][27]:
1. **LLM request layer** — sends requests through centralized gateway
2. **Usage logging service** — records token counts, model, cost per request
3. **Budget manager** — tracks spending against limits in real-time
4. **Alerting/enforcement system** — graduated responses from alerts to blocking

Every request must carry metadata (user_id, feature_name, team) for attribution.
Without per-request cost breakdowns, it is impossible to determine which features,
users, or workflows drive highest spend [23].

### Langfuse

Two tracking methods [24]:
- **Ingestion**: Direct capture from LLM response (prioritized when available)
- **Inference**: Automatic via model parameter using built-in tokenizers

Supports pricing tiers with regex patterns and comparison operators (e.g.,
Claude Sonnet 4.5 charges higher rates above 200K input tokens). Custom model
definitions via UI/API. OpenRouter and LiteLLM integrations capture
provider-specific costs automatically [24].

### OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions

Standard schema for LLM monitoring [25]:
- Tracks: temperature, top_p, model name/version, token counts, cost
- Request/response data as span events (not attributes) to avoid bloated spans
- Three metric categories: request volume, request duration, cost/token counters
- OpenLIT provides auto-instrumentation with Grafana dashboards

## Budget Enforcement Strategies

### Graduated Response Model

| Budget Threshold | Action |
|-----------------|--------|
| 50% | Alerts to stakeholders [23] |
| 80% | Throttle non-critical agents [23] |
| 90% | Downgrade to cheaper models [23] |
| 95% | Pause everything except approved workflows [23] |
| 100% | Block all requests (last resort) [23] |

### Three-Layer Governance (Cordum)

**Layer 1: Per-Action** — cap tokens per LLM call, enforce timeouts, kill calls
exceeding thresholds [23]

**Layer 2: Per-Agent** — time-windowed budgets (e.g., research agent: $50/hour).
Agent pauses when exhausted, catches runaway loops [23]

**Layer 3: Fleet-Level** — monitor total spend across all agents with graceful
degradation [23]

### Policy-as-Code

Version-controlled YAML policies enforced before execution [23]:
- Throttle rules: rate-limit expensive operations (20/hour, 3 concurrent max)
- Approval gates: human review for operations >$50 estimated cost
- Deny rules: block unbounded recursive agent loops
- Allow rules: pass through cached reads with no overhead
- Per-topic timeouts: research 120s, drafting 60s, enrichment 30s

### Cost Escalation Example

3 parallel agents × 5 sub-calls × 50K tokens × $0.015/1K = $11.25/round.
20 rounds × 10 batches/day = $2,250/day or $10K in 4.5 days [23].

Agent autonomy amplifies cost multiplicatively through fan-out, retries, long
contexts, and concurrency [23].

## Framework-Level Cost Tracking

| Framework | Tracking Method | Budget Controls |
|-----------|----------------|-----------------|
| LangGraph | Via Langfuse/LangSmith integration | Token/time budgets in config |
| AutoGen/AG2 | `print_usage_summary()`, `gather_usage_summary()` [26] | Inference + optimization budgets in $/1K tokens [34] |
| CrewAI | Built-in tracking | `max_tokens`, `max_execution_time` [33] |

AG2 supports custom per-model pricing via config: `"price": [prompt_cost,
completion_cost]` per 1K tokens. Azure OpenAI defaults to gpt-3.5-turbo-0125
pricing when version info unavailable [26].

## Cost Optimization Stack

| Technique | Savings | When to Use |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| Prompt caching (Anthropic) | Up to 90% on reads [17] | Repetitive prefixes, multi-turn |
| Batch API | 50%+ [27] | Non-urgent workloads |
| Smart routing | 30-85% [61] | Multi-provider setups |
| Semantic caching | Up to 73% [27] | High-frequency similar queries |
| Combined strategies | 70-90% total [55] | All production systems |

Real-world: monthly spend from $720 to $72 after enabling caching [50]. 31% of
LLM queries exhibit semantic similarity to previous requests [50].

## The "Cheapest Model" Paradox

Selecting the lowest per-token cost often backfires. A more capable model may
produce correct output on the first attempt, requiring fewer iterations and less
total token consumption [27]. Optimize for unit economics of the use case
(total cost to achieve outcome), not raw token price [27].

## Gaps and Limitations

- No standard for cost attribution metadata schemas beyond basic user/feature tags
- Real-time budget enforcement latency overhead is not well benchmarked
- Multi-provider billing reconciliation tools are immature
- Cache hit rate benchmarks across application types are sparse
- OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions are still evolving and adoption is early
